title: Annotatio I §.I: Not priority of Dignity or Order (Sennert) — but of Time and Acerbitas
pass_a_gloss: Namely they are heard as prior, not by priority of Dignity — because they concern some fundamental article of the Christian faith, or a principal one of those brought back under the anvil of disputations by Protestants and among themselves; nor by Priority of Order — because in a Methodical treatment of Protestant Controversies, that is disposed according to the natural method of the Theological System, they would deserve first place. For even some of the Lutherans will deprecate these species of priority, by many reasons collected into one by And. Sennert, Theological Exercises on the fundamental articles of faith §§. 64 & 65, pp. 430 & 431 of his Fascicle of exercises.
pass_b_english: They are not “prior” by dignity — as if they alone were some fundamental article of the faith, or the chief matter Protestants hammer out among themselves.
Nor by order — as if a methodical theological system would have to put them first.
Even some Lutherans deprecate those kinds of priority (Sennert, Exercises on fundamental articles §§. 64–65, fasc. pp. 430–431).
source_text: Scilicet priores audiunt, non prioritate Dignitatis, quòd fundamentalem quendam fidei Christianae articulum, aut principalem istorum concernunt qui sub disputationes incudem à Protestantibus, & inter se, revocantur; nec Prioritate Ordinis, quòd in Methodica, id est, juxta naturalem Systematis Theologici methodum disposita Controversiarum Protestanticarum tractatione, primum locum mererentur. Has enim prioritatis species vel Lutheranorum nonnulli deprecabuntur, per rationes plurimas ab And. Sennerto in unum collectas, Exerc. Theol. de articulis fid. fundamentalibus §. 64. & 65. p. Fasciculi exercitationum ejus 430. & 431.
